source.title: The Mythical Man-Month in the Age of AI
source.author: ilreb

excerpt.zh: AI代理让软件协作更快，却没有消除布鲁克斯定律：需求不清时，更多代理可能只是更快地产生错误答案。
excerpt.en: AI agents speed up software work, but Brooks’s Law still applies: unclear requirements can make teams reach the wrong answer faster.

disclosure.zh: 本文使用星期天AI中转站大模型，基于 Hacker News 内容自动生成。
disclosure.en: This article was automatically generated by the Weekly Day AI gateway model using content from Hacker News.

text.zh: AI代理重新解释布鲁克斯定律
AI代理正在改变软件项目中的分工，但它并没有让布鲁克斯定律失效。该定律源自弗雷德里克·布鲁克斯对大型软件项目的经验，核心观点是：给延期的软件项目增加人手，可能会让项目更晚完成。如今，代理可以迅速获取上下文，也不需要传统团队中的培训、会议和日常协调。
text.en: AI agents are changing how software projects divide work, but they have not made Brooks’s Law obsolete. Based on Frederick Brooks’s experience with large software projects, the law holds that adding people to a late project can make it later. Agents can absorb context quickly and avoid much of the training, meeting, and routine coordination required by human teams.

text.zh: 瓶颈从人员协调转向代理编排
text.en: The Bottleneck Moves to Agent Orchestration

text.zh: 文章指出，真正困难的部分仍然存在。某些任务必须按顺序完成，多个代理也无法把一个月的连续工作压缩成一天。项目负责人仍需定义“完成”、审查代码、识别幻觉，并把不同代理的产出整合起来。若缺少清晰的编排，代理甚至可能反复覆盖彼此的修改，增加返工。
text.en: The difficult parts remain. Some tasks are inherently sequential, so multiple agents cannot compress a month of continuous work into a single day. Someone still has to define what “done” means, review code, detect hallucinations, and combine the agents’ outputs. Without clear orchestration, agents may repeatedly overwrite one another’s changes and create more rework.

text.zh: 更快得到答案，也可能更快走错
text.en: Faster Answers Can Still Be Wrong

text.zh: 这带来一个重要限制：AI代理减少的可能是部分协作成本，而不是需求不确定性、验证责任或系统复杂度。文章提出，面向代理时代的布鲁克斯定律可以改写为：“向需求不清的项目增加代理，只会更快得到错误答案。”这句话仍是概括性的判断；代理在实际项目中的收益，取决于任务是否可并行、要求是否明确，以及人类能否有效审查结果。
text.en: The key limitation is that AI agents may reduce some coordination costs without removing ambiguity, verification responsibility, or system complexity. The article’s proposed update is: “Adding agents to a project with unclear requirements gets you the wrong answer faster.” That remains a concise rule of thumb; real gains depend on whether work can be parallelized, whether requirements are clear, and whether people can review the results effectively.
